runs.text: THE 4TH COMMANDMENT:
1. In what important document in the Bible do we learn about the Sabbath?
Exodus 20:8
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Note:
In God’s eyes, the Sabbath is very important. It is so important that He placed it in the heart of the Ten Commandments. The fourth commandment tells us to remember the Sabbath day.
2. According to the fourth commandment, to whom does the Sabbath belong?
Exodus 20:10
But
the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God
: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates.
Note:
All through the Bible, both Old and New Testaments, we find that the Sabbath belongs to God and not man. Yes, it was made for man, but it does not belong to man. (See also Exodus 31:13)
3. According to the prophet Isaiah, whose holy day is the Sabbath?
Isaiah 58:13
If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure
on my holy day.
Note:

Many people think that it is okay to just pick one day in seven as their Sabbath. Is this okay? The answer is that we are commanded in the Ten Commandments to keep God’s Sabbath. We are not commanded to keep our own day. God’s Sabbath points to God as the source of all righteousness in our lives. Man choosing his own day is man thinking that he can lift his own self from the degradation of sin.
The true Sabbath is a surrendering of our will to God’s will. Choosing a day of our own is interposing a perverse will and frustrating God’s grace. God says to remember His Sabbath, not our day.
4. What promise does God make to those who keep His Sabbath holy?
Isaiah 58:13

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:

Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it.
Note:

God loves it when we surrender our will to Him. If we insist on saving ourselves, we will be disappointed in the end. Isaiah describes a people who speak their own words, insisting on their own way. Many today find their “own pleasure” by keeping their own day in direct opposition to God’s expressed will. Isaiah also describes the blessings that God sends to those who keep His Sabbath day. God causes them to ride on the high places of the earth. God’s blessing attends those who follow Him by resting on His seventh-day Sabbath.
THE SABBATH IS GOD’S SIGN (SEAL) OF A PERPETUAL COVENANT:
5. Of what else is the Sabbath a sign?
Exodus 31:16
Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.
It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested
, and was refreshed.
Note:

It is important to know that the Sabbath is a sign of God’s creative ability. We would not see evolution slowly creeping into the Christian church if we weekly worshiped Him who made the heavens and the earth as stated in the fourth commandment. The Sabbath is a sign forever, a perpetual covenant. This means that the Sabbath will be the sign of the redeemed forever.
THE SABBATH AND CREATION:
6. Why did God rest on the seventh day of creation and sanctify it?
Genesis 1:31
And
God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.
And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
Note:

There are two reasons why God rested on the seventh day of creation. The first reason was because all that He had created was “very good”. (See Genesis 1:31) The second was because “the heavens and the earth were finished”. (See Genesis 2:1) Therefore, the reason God rested and set aside the seventh day was to commemorate a perfect and finished work.
7. For whom did Jesus say the Sabbath was made?
Mark 2:27
And he said unto them,
The sabbath was made for man
, and not man for the sabbath.
Note:

God’s design is for the Sabbath to be a special blessing for man. On this day we set aside our daily toil and worship God as our Creator. We are to relax from our anxieties and to trust and know our loving Father.
8. Upon which day of the week were Adam and Eve created?
Genesis 1:27
So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. 31 And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.
And the evening and the morning were the sixth day
Note:
Adam was created at the end of the sixth day. This means that God’s Sabbath was really Adam’s first whole day. So, when we consider the Sabbath from God’s point of view, God had us begin by resting.
Adam and Eve began by being completely God-dependent. This order becomes significant when we consider the Sabbath in light of the next question.
9. What did God say to Adam after the fall?
Genesis 3:19
In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread,
till thou return unto the ground.
Note:
When Adam and Eve sinned, they turned their backs on God and became self-dependent. That is why, after the fall, God said they would eat their bread by the sweat of their brow.
A SIGN OF SANCTIFICATION:
10. What is the sign of sanctification?
Exodus 31:13
Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying,
Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign
between me and you throughout your generations;
that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you.
Note:

In his natural flesh, man cannot keep the Ten Commandments. But this same law that we fail in keeping is the standard of Christian righteousness. When we walk in the Spirit, God produces fruit in our lives. This fruit is the love that enables man to walk in harmony with God’s Commandments. (See Romans 13:8-10) This process is called sanctification. The Sabbath is a sign that it is God who sanctifies us. The Sabbath is a sign that it is God who makes us holy.

Often those who keep the seventh day Sabbath are accused of legalism. Legalism describes a person who believes that they are saved by keeping the law instead of by the grace of God. Unfortunately, this accusation does indeed fit some seventh day Sabbath keepers. But it does not have to be this way! True Sabbath observance is the polar opposite of legalism. True Sabbath observance is remembering the Sabbath as a sign between God and man that it is God who sanctifies us by faith, not our legalism.

Isn’t it wonderful to know that God’s Sabbath is a weekly reminder of who gets the credit for the good works in our lives? Sabbath is a reminder that it is God who sanctifies us, not our own good works. (See Exodus 31:13)
11. Which day is the Sabbath?
Exodus 20:10
But
the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God:
in it thou shalt not do any work.
Note:

The Sabbath is celebrated on the seventh day of the weekly cycle. History teaches us that a change was made from Saturday to Sunday on March 7, 321 AD. This change was made almost 300 years after the death of Christ. There are no Bible texts that even hint of God changing His Sabbath day to Sunday. Saturday is still the Sabbath day. When men changed the Sabbath day, they changed one of God’s Ten Commandments. God does not change! So, when men change God’s expressed command they become self-dependent instead of being God-dependent.
ENTERING GOD’S REST:
12. To what secret place or abode was God trying to bring Israel after they left Egypt?
Exodus 3:17
And I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt unto the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites,
unto a land flowing with milk and honey
Note:

God promised Israel a land flowing with milk and honey where God would meet all their needs. God provided all of Israel’s needs in the desert. God provided their water (See Numbers 20:11), He provided their food from manna (See Exodus 16:14), He even provided their clothing. Their shoes and clothing did not wear out for 40 years (See Deuteronomy 8:4, 29:5). We too are meant to be God-dependent! God will meet all of our needs when we depend completely on Him.
13. Why did God say that Israel could not enter his rest?
Hebrews 3:17
But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them ... whose carcases fell in the wilderness? 18;
And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
Note:
They could not enter the promised land because of unbelief.
14. Who had disobeyed the gospel?
Romans 10:16
But they have not all
obeyed the gospel
. For Esaias saith,
Lord, who hath believed our report?
Note:
The Bible uses the words obey and believe interchangeably. We obey God when we become totally God-dependent.
15. Can we fall short of God’s promise of entering His rest?
Hebrews 4:1
Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
Note:
The Jews fell short of God’s promise of rest. We can also fall short of the promise.
16. How do we enter His rest today?
Hebrews 4:2
For unto us was
the gospel
preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not
being mixed with faith
in them that heard it.
Note:

God’s restful abode is linked to the gospel. The Everlasting Gospel offers a complete rest in the work of Christ. We can only enter this rest by ceasing from our own works of the flesh. Our fallen flesh is not capable of producing good works that are in harmony with God’s law. Yet this very law is what we will be judged by. (See James 2:12) (See also Revelation 22:14)
17. Since there remains a rest for us to enter, what are we to do to enter?
Hebrews 4:9
There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
10 For he that is entered into his rest, he also
hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his
Note:
We enter His rest by doing something that may be harder than any other test. We enter this restful place as Christians by ceasing our masquerade of “fake good works” of the flesh.

The word “Rest” is from the Greek word (#4520 Sabbatismos). It is only used once in scripture. Israel failed to enter His rest. Therefore, there remains a Sabbatismos (keeping of Sabbath) for the people of God.
18. Why doesn’t it do any good to add our own good works to enter into His rest?
Hebrews 4:3
For we which have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although
the works were finished from the foundation of the world
Note:

There is nothing for us to add to God’s finished work, because the works of God have been finished since the foundation of the world. It is, therefore, a sin for us to add our futile efforts of the flesh to what God has already accomplished. The Sabbath is ceasing our own self-righteous works and trusting in God’s finished work.
19. What day does the Bible speak of as an example of this rest from our efforts?
Hebrews 4:4
For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise,
And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.
Note:

God is using His Sabbath as an example of how we are to enter His rest. God rested from all His works. We are to believe by faith in God’s provision. His rest is like a secret place, or an abode we can enter into. Nothing of this world can enter and harm us there. God will take care of all of our needs. The Sabbath is a sign that it is God alone, by faith, who makes us holy (Sanctified).
20. What is the Sabbath a sign of?
Ezekiel 20:12
Moreover also
I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the LORD that sanctify them.
Note:

God sanctifies us through His Spirit. The only way for God to sanctify us through His Spirit is for us to have complete trust in Him. Just as justification by faith has the sign of baptism, the Sabbath is the sign of sanctification. No one is saved by baptism, or keeping Sabbath. We are saved by the blood of God’s dear Son. Remembering the Sabbath is our response to the good fruit that God is performing in our lives by faith.
“The Sabbath is a sign of Christ’s power to make us holy. And it is given to all whom Christ makes holy as a sign of His sanctifying power.”
21. How long will God perform His work in us?
Philippians 1:6
Being confident of this very thing, that
he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ.
Note:
We can be confident that God will perform a good work in us until the end. It is safe to enter His secret abode. The Sabbath is a weekly reminder that we can trust Him to sanctify us by faith.
22. Let us, therefore, labour to do what?
Hebrews 4:11
Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.
Note:

Why not begin this complete trust in God’s love today. Let’s stop trying to enter by our own works of the flesh. Let us be diligent to have faith in His ability to sanctify us. Let us die to self and the lust of our flesh, and exercise faith in God’s ability to sanctify us by remembering the 7th day, and cooperating with the good works (fruit) that He is performing in our hearts.
23. In the new earth, what will the redeemed do every Sabbath?
Isaiah 66:22
For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the LORD, so shall your seed and your name remain.
And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD
Note:

The Sabbath has never been changed or stopped. In fact, the redeemed will worship before the Lord from one Sabbath to another in God’s kingdom. This means that the redeemed will keep God’s Sabbath forever.
24. Will Sabbath be kept during the tribulation?
Matthew 24:20
But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day:
For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.
Note:
God’s true people will still be keeping the Sabbath at the end of time.
SABBATH FOR THE JEWS ONLY?
25. Question: Wasn’t the Sabbath for the Jews only?
Genesis 2:2
And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.
Note:

The first Sabbath was instituted and kept by God on the seventh day of creation. The Sabbath was instituted thousands of years before the first Jew ever existed. The Sabbath was also instituted before sin entered the world. Therefore, Christians who observe the seventh day today keep a Creation Sabbath as a sign that it is God who makes them holy, not a Jewish Sabbath.
26. Wasn’t the Sabbath for the Jews only because it is first mentioned in scripture to be kept when God gave the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai?
Exodus 19:1
In the third month, when the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egyp
t, the same day came they into the wilderness of Sinai.
Note:

The Ten Commandments were given from Mount Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt. We will notice in question #27 that God tested Israel two weeks earlier on the 15th day of the second month. God tested Israel on the Sabbath question before He gave the Ten Commandments on Sinai! (See Exodus 16:1-5) God tested the people before there even was an old covenant.
27. On What date did God test Israel, whether they would keep His law?
Exodus 16:1
And they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai,
on the fifteenth day of the second month
after their departing out of the land of Egypt. 4 Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day,
that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no
And it shall come to pass, that on the sixth day they shall prepare that which they bring in; and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily
Note:

We find that God proved (tested) Israel at least two weeks earlier in the second month. He tested them on whether they would gather a double portion of manna on the 6th day. The 6th day was called the Preparation Day. It was a day used to prepare for the weekly Sabbath. So Israel knew about the preparation day before the Ten Commandments were given to Israel.

When God tested Israel’s faith, He tested to see whether they would keep His day Holy. When God tested Adam and Eve in the Garden, it was the simplest of tests. It was not something terribly hard that was almost impossible to do. God loved them and gave them something easy. Soon at the end of time, there will be a test. The test will be on whether we will receive God’s seal, showing dependence on Him alone, or whether we will follow men and receive the Mark of the Beast. The Mark of the Beast is about who we worship. (See Revelation 14:9-10) As the scroll of time is unrolled we will be able to discern additional insights as to the beast’s actual mark.

The Bible is clear, God’s holy day is the seventh day. But man has instituted other days. Christians keep Sunday in celebration of the resurrection, even though there are no Bible texts to support this change.

If the Sabbath had never been changed from Saturday to Sunday, if all Christians still kept God’s original seventh day, it would be almost impossible to convince any of them from the Bible alone to keep a different day than God’s seventh day.
Muslims pray to Allah on Friday. In Islamic countries Saturday is called ﺳﺒﺖ, Sabt (cognate to Sabbath.)
28. How do we keep the Sabbath?
Exodus 20:10
But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God:
in it thou shalt not do any work.
Note:
Adam’s test in the garden was not some difficult task that was almost impossible to do. He was tested on not doing something. God was not asking Adam to accomplish some impossible task.
God does not change. (See Malachi 3:6) Today, He is asking us to remember the 7th day. (See Exodus 20:7) This is for our benefit. Which day will you remember?
29. Who changed the Sabbath Day from Saturday to Sunday?
Daniel 7:25
And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High,
and think to change times and laws:
and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.
Note:

The Catholic Church claims that she made the change from Sabbath to Sunday. Over the years she has even boasted of making the change: Please ask yourself this question: Does a church have the right to change one of the Ten Commandments? Of course not! By changing God’s law men are trying to enter heaven by doing things man’s own way.
“The Catholic Church, … by virtue of her divine mission, changed the day from Saturday to Sunday” (The Catholic Mirror, official publication of James Cardinal Gibbons, Sept. 23, 1893).
Protestants do not realize that by observing Sunday, they accept the authority of the spokesperson of the Church, the Pope” (Our Sunday Visitor, February 5, 1950).
The Catholic Church claims that “the church is above the Bible, and this transference of Sabbath observance is proof of that fact” (Catholic Record of London, Ontario Sept 1, 1923).
